title: AISI cyber-eval reciprocity locks in as allied procurement gate by Q3 2026
body: By Q3 2026 the May 8 reciprocity-perimeter expansion — Singapore IMDA + Japan AISI publishing a parallel memorandum-of-cooperation accepting AISI-administered TLO-range cyber-evaluation runs as satisfying their respective frontier-model voluntary-disclosure regimes (120-day placement window) inside 24 hours of the May 7 EU-UK joint memorandum, with Canada CCCS and Australia ASD ACSC pre-committing to mirror language by Q3 2026 and the Mythos + GPT-5.5 results cited as the operational threshold — combined with HM Treasury's same-day extension of the public-sector LLM-coding-assistant procurement pause to a 30-day formal review naming Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini Code Assist, and Microsoft GitHub Copilot for Government tenants in a temporarily-suspended-vendors annex pending Mythos-class capability disclosure under the AI Procurement Common Standard, force the AISI-administered cyber-evaluation regime to consolidate as the operative gating criterion for sovereign + allied public-sector AI procurement across at least six jurisdictions before Q3 2026 closes. The forcing function is that once Singapore IMDA + Japan AISI lift the EU-UK template into the Indo-Pacific within one news cycle and a Five Eyes member (UK) names the Big-4 frontier-lab + hyperscaler-coding-assistant cohort by vendor in a procurement-freeze annex, the absence of a parallel US recognition pathway converts the FMRB executive order draft from a domestic-disclosure question into a market-access question for US-based labs. The most likely shape is a six-or-seven-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter (UK + EU + Singapore + Japan + Canada + Australia, with New Zealand or South Korea as the seventh) treating an AISI-administered cyber-eval pass as a per-tenant Mythos-class capability disclosure, paired with a UK + EU + at-least-one-Indo-Pacific allied named-vendor procurement-gate annex tied to that pass. Bear case is that the FMRB EO ships first with §708-equivalent reciprocal recognition language and short-circuits the multilateral path; absent that, Q3 2026 lands the perimeter as the operative procurement gate.

reasoning.because: Singapore IMDA + Japan AISI publish reciprocity MoC May 8 within 24 hours of EU-UK joint memorandum.
reasoning.given: HM Treasury 30-day freeze names Big-4 frontier-lab + coding-assistant vendors.
reasoning.so_that: AISI cyber-eval reciprocity perimeter consolidates as the gating criterion for allied sovereign AI procurement.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; six-or-seven jurisdictions; second named-vendor annex.
reasoning.plain_language: Britain, the EU, Singapore, and Japan agreed to share AI safety tests; allies will copy the rule for buying AI.

summary: Singapore IMDA and Japan AISI sign a cyber-eval reciprocity MoC within 24 hours of the EU-UK joint memorandum, while HM Treasury extends a 30-day procurement freeze naming Big-4 frontier-lab vendors. By Q3 2026 AISI cyber-eval reciprocity locks in as the allied-procurement gate.
